messages:
sara_support: opening this thread — customer reported repeated POSTs for the same order when they hit transient 502/429s, and now they see duplicate charges. attaching the sanitized request/response logs below.

sara_support: logs (redacted):
```
POST /v1/orders  2023-11-12T14:02:09Z  idempotency-key: none
-> 502 Bad Gateway
client retry after ~200ms -> 200 OK (order created)
client retry after ~400ms -> 200 OK (order created again)
```

sara_support: customer says they used our JS SDK with default config, no idempotency header set. they expect sdk to avoid re-sending non-idempotent requests automatically. any guidance?

carla_se: ugh, yep, classic. do we know which exact SDK version? asking because we recently changed retry defaults on 1.x -> 2.x.

sara_support: they are on `@redwood/sdk-js 1.4.2` (came from support ticket).

lucas_sdk: fwiw, SDK 1.x defaults: retries on network errors and 5xxs + 429, exponential backoff with full jitter, maxRetries=5. not idempotency-aware. this was to be lenient for flaky networks but iirc it caused exactly this in some POST-heavy integrations.

max_engineer: ok, some quick notes from runtime: our edge sometimes returns 502 for backend timeouts during bursts; if a client retries too aggressively you can easily get multiple downstream writes. we do send `Retry-After` for 429s when quota-based, but the SDK's backoff may ignore it unless configured to honor server headers.

sara_support: customer asks two things: (1) how to get refunds for duplicated orders quickly, and (2) how to stop this from happening again w/o forcing them to rewrite code.

billing_bot: FYI: we have a manual duplicate charge refund flow. I've created ticket BILL-5621 for this customer; finance will process refunds once support confirms duplicates. link: https://billing.example.com/t/BILL-5621 :white_check_mark:

carla_se: for the immediate stopgap, tell them to set `retry: { maxRetries: 0 }` in the SDK config OR pass an idempotency key on write ops. code sample to share:```js
import Redwood from '@redwood/sdk-js';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY, retry: { maxRetries: 0 } });
// or
client.orders.create({ body }, { headers: { 'Idempotency-Key': 'client-uuid-1234' } });
```

lucas_sdk: longer term we should change SDK defaults: only retry non-idempotent mutating calls if caller provides an idempotency key OR if the endpoint is explicitly documented as safe-to-retry. Proposed default behavior (RFC in one line): `mutations: maxRetries=0 unless Idempotency-Key header present; reads: existing policy`. Thoughts?

max_engineer: +1. also respect `Retry-After` and server-provided `x-rw-quota-reset` if present. and low default retry count (<=2) for idempotent retries even when key present.

ops_oncall: we also need guidance on server side rate limit signals. please include these in the reply: we return `429` for quota exceeded and `503`/`502` when backend overloaded. 429 will include `Retry-After` when rate-limited; quota burst rejections include `x-rw-remaining` and `x-rw-reset`. if client ignores those and retries fast, they're causing a thundering herd.

sara_support: writing back to customer: immediate steps + rationale. will paste draft here, pls quick review:

--- draft reply to customer ---
Hi — sorry about the duplicate orders. we can refund the duplicates right away (BILL-5621). the root cause looks like client retries after transient errors (502/429) without an idempotency key so the same operation was executed more than once.
Quick mitigation options:
1) Set `retry: { maxRetries: 0 }` in the SDK configuration (no code changes beyond config).
2) Attach an `Idempotency-Key` header (UUID) to order-create requests — the SDK will dedupe when this header is present.
3) If you need retries + safety, upgrade to the SDK `2.x` beta (has idempotency-aware retry toggles) or we can backport a small patch to 1.x with `retriesOnMutations=false` config.
We recommend option 2 for production: it preserves client durability while avoiding duplicates.
--- end draft ---

carla_se: looks good. add a short repro we can run internally to reproduce the double-write quickly.

sara_support: repro steps I'll include:
1) `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/orders -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"item":"A"}' --silent -D -`
2) introduce an artificial 502 by hitting the backend via `RUNTIME_TEST_MODE=slow` env on a test account (ops can provide flag)
3) run a simple loop with retry enabled (client waits 200ms then retry) -> you'll see 2 created orders.

max_engineer: adding exact command for the repro load generator (internal only):
```
for i in 1..50; do curl -s -X POST https://staging-api.redwood.ai/v1/orders -H "Idempotency-Key: "$(uuidgen) -d '{"item":"A"}' &
done
```
Note: remove Idempotency-Key to reproduce duplicate writes.

lucas_sdk: i'm going to open a small patch PR for the SDK:
- change 1.x to default `mutations.maxRetries=0`
- add an explicit opt-in `retryOnMutation: true` that requires `Idempotency-Key` to be present
- document server `Retry-After` handling and how SDK honors it
I'll link PR when ready.

ops_oncall: once PR is up, let's also add a runtime banner in the Console docs about quota signals and recommend client configs. ops can provide `RUNTIME_TEST_MODE` for internal repro.

sara_support: next steps (action items):
- billing_bot coordinate refund (BILL-5621) — billing_bot
- SDK patch PR — lucas_sdk
- ops provide `RUNTIME_TEST_MODE` flag and run repro with support — ops_oncall
- update support KB article for duplicate charges + recommended SDK config — carla_se/sara_support

billing_bot: confirmed — finance will start refund flow once support replies with charge IDs.

sara_support: thanks all — i'll send the draft to the customer in ~15m with the short repro and the immediate config change suggestion. will paste the final message here. :thumbsup:

lucas_sdk: PR: https://github.com/redwood/sdk-js/pull/412 (draft) — includes unit tests and a migration note. asking for review from @max_engineer for server headers handling.

max_engineer: reviewing now. agree on the conservative defaults. also can we add a telemetry event `mutation_retry_attempt` so we can track how often clients retry mutating ops in the wild? helps product/finance triage duplicates.

lucas_sdk: good call, i'll add telemetry.

sara_support: final customer reply sent. closing internal thread after refunds confirmed. thanks everyone.
